subject: Capacity continuity addendum request — reserved GPU preemption carveouts
messages:
From: Anika Bose <anika.bose@heliosretail.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity continuity for peak sales event — request for preemption carveout

Hi Mateo,

We just finished our modeling for the November 2025 holiday push and the traffic curves look steeper than last year. We had a scheduled dry run last weekend and observed several brief latency spikes tied to what our team believes are GPU preemptions on your dedicated pool — during those windows our checkout latency spiked ~800ms and throughput dropped sharply for small bursts (attached logs).

Helios is evaluating a multiyear reserved capacity commitment, but before we sign we need assurance that during one 72-hour peak window a year (approximate dates: Black Friday week) we can request a preemption carveout or a continuity addendum so our reserved nodes won’t be forcibly rebalanced mid-window. The key asks from our side:
- A guaranteed no-preemption window for up to 72 hours, initiated with 48hrs notice
- A throughput continuity SLO (p90 tail latency and sustained throughput target) for that window; if missed, financial credits or make-goods
- A contactable escalation path if we see degradation

Can Redwood provide either a commercial/contract addendum that documents this, or a technical mitigation we can sign up to (e.g., a reserved subset of nodes that are isolated from preemption)? We attached logs and a short timeline.

Thanks — would like to discuss with your team this week.

Best,
Anika Bose

Thanks for the context. Short technical summary and options: 

1) Strict non-preemption window (hard carveout):
   - Feasible only if Helios holds a true dedicated subset of instances that are statically pinned for the window. No preemption, no eviction.
   - Impact: requires us to hold that capacity out of the pool for the entire reserved term or dynamically reserve extra headroom. Operational cost: ~30–50% additional reserved capacity during the year to keep flexibility for other customers.

2) Soft-priority continuity (recommended default):
   - During the notified window, Helios gets elevated scheduling priority and a guaranteed minimum token of concurrent slots (e.g., 80% of baseline). Preemption can still occur for infra emergencies, but we commit runbook steps and escalations and offer credits for regression against SLO.
   - Lower cost to Helios than hard carveout. Requires a documented grace/backoff policy and a fast escalation path to ops.

3) Priority queue + model variant fallback:
   - We can reserve a small hot-standby pool and route latency-sensitive requests to a lower-cost low-latency quantized variant if core capacity is constrained. This reduces the severity of tail spikes but may have small differences in token quality.

For Helios' ask (72 hrs once a year) my recommendation: soft-priority continuity with an optional hard carveout for a capped number of slots (e.g., up to X GPUs) if they are willing to commit to 1.5x of their nominal reserved commitment for the contract year. We can define the SLO as: during the continuity window, 95% of requests served at <= 200ms additional token latency over baseline and sustained RPS within 90% of the pre-declared threshold. If breached, credit equals N hours * agreed $/hour.

I attached the internal_preemption_runbook.md and a short table of estimated headroom and cost deltas for Helios' current footprint.

– Karthik

Subject: Re: Capacity continuity addendum request — draft and next steps

Thanks everyone — happy to own the commercial draft. Per Karthik's guidance, here's the contract approach I propose:

1) Scope: define a single annual "Continuity Window" up to 72 consecutive hours. Customer may request up to two windows per year with 48hrs notice; additional windows require written agreement.
2) Modes: (a) Soft-priority continuity (default, no extra cost, commits to minimum throughput token share), (b) Hard carveout (optional, requires an up-front capacity uplift commit and higher fees).
3) Measurements: SLO expressed as p90 request latency and sustained RPS baseline; measurement methodology referenced to per-route telemetry in Redwood Console.
4) Remedies: Service credits calculated hourly for breach: 5% credit per hour breach up to 100% of window fees, or make-good capacity time offered at equivalent value.
5) Initiation/Termination: 48hr initiation notice; Redwood may terminate carveout only for declared infra emergency with Customer notified and credit applied.

Next steps: I will update the redwood_capacity_addendum_draft.pdf with these two-mode options and draft language for the GTC addendum. Mateo — please confirm the rough headroom/cost numbers Karthik recommended and I'll include them as an appendix. Anika — if this aligns I can produce a redlined addendum for Helios to review by EOD Friday.

Marissa Cole
